meta.label: Sleep opportunity
meta.rationale: Computed from several measurements; inherits their confidence.

text: Opportunity is time in bed: when you switched the light off and when you got up. It is the half of sleep you actually control, and the half the ring measures best, since bedtime and waketime are direct timing rather than inferred sleep. Your target is 8h in bed, lights out 11:27 pm tonight.
Across your history each extra hour in bed has bought about 48 minutes of actual sleep, and that rate barely falls at the top of the range — which is the whole reason this metric exists.

Worth knowing rather than worrying about: 8h in bed yields roughly 7.0h of sleep at your 88% efficiency, against a sleep need of 7.41h. Clearing this debt entirely still leaves about 22 minutes a night of sleep debt. Full need would want 8.4h in bed; the lower target is deliberate, because you meet it far more often and a target you keep beats a target you admire.
This page is the nightly version: how much more or less time in bed you gave yourself than the target.
